headline: Vermont opens $300,000 grant path for teacher apprenticeships
dek: The new program will help educator-preparation providers build paid, debt-reducing routes to Vermont licensure, with applications due Feb. 23, 2027.
body: Vermont is making $300,000 available to expand teacher registered-apprenticeship programs, a new funding opportunity aimed at helping educator-preparation providers build debt-reducing routes into the profession. The [Vermont Agency of Education](https://education.vermont.gov/news/grow-your-own-teacher-registered-apprenticeship-expansion-grant) announced the competitive subgrant Sept. 29 with the Vermont Department of Labor and the National Center for Grow Your Own, which will administer the application and award process.

The grant is intended for programs that combine educator preparation with employment and supervised classroom experience. The Agency of Education says the opportunity is designed to create or expand Teacher Registered Apprenticeship Programs across the state, with particular attention to rural, high-need and underserved communities, including areas beyond Vermont's current apprenticeship model. That focus matters in a state where recruiting and retaining licensed teachers is harder for small districts that compete across long distances and have fewer preparation options nearby.

Individual awards may reach $100,000 per distinct proposal. Vermont-approved educator-preparation providers may lead an application, including approved colleges and universities and approved alternative-route providers that have a university or credit partner. Out-of-state providers may participate as well. Each proposal must include at least one Vermont local education agency that will employ the apprentices and their assigned mentors, according to the Agency of Education's grant notice.

The money is not a general scholarship pool for people who want to become teachers. It is intended to cover approved apprentice tuition, required fees and books for a complete pathway to initial Vermont licensure. The state says grant funds and other available resources must ensure that selected apprentices pay nothing out of pocket for those costs. The arrangement can allow a school employee, such as a paraeducator, to earn while receiving training and moving toward a teaching license, although the grant notice does not promise a job or admission to any particular preparation program.

The new round builds on a Vermont apprenticeship system that has already tested teacher pathways. In its [2024 workforce report](https://legislature.vermont.gov/assets/Legislative-Reports/Workforce-Investment-System-Registered-Apprenticeship-Program-Annual-Report-2024.pdf), the Department of Labor said a federal State Apprenticeship Expansion Fund grant helped the Vermont Rural Education Collaborative work with school districts, the Agency of Education and other partners. That effort registered seven pre-K through grade 12 teacher-apprenticeship programs and had 28 apprentices in the program as of summer 2024. The same report said the Agency of Education had identified more than 1,300 teachers working on provisional or emergency licenses in April 2023, a dated measure of the staffing challenge rather than a current count.

The prior model centered on Vermont's Northeast Kingdom and used a hybrid structure: apprentices with bachelor's degrees in fields other than education worked under provisional or emergency licenses, received mentoring and completed online coursework and competency-based portfolios. The new grant is statewide and can support both new and existing programs, so its effect will depend on which providers apply and which districts are prepared to employ and mentor apprentices.

Prospective applicants can attend a pre-proposal conference Oct. 7 from 2 to 3 p.m. Eastern, with additional sessions scheduled for Oct. 21, Nov. 4 and Jan. 13. Applications are due Feb. 23, 2027. The Agency of Education directs questions to the [National Center for Grow Your Own](https://ncgyo.org/vermont), whose grant page says the $300,000 allocation comes from an education grant to the organization from Ascendium Education Group. The immediate next step is therefore planning: providers and districts must decide whether they can meet the partnership, licensure and no-out-of-pocket requirements before submitting a proposal.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: Vermont's new $300,000 teacher-apprenticeship grant supports educator-preparation providers and rural school districts.
